canonical_data: in-memory agent action history and run output from a Node script or test run; the README documents no durable store
strengths: Acts on screenshots by pixel coordinates instead of numbered DOM boxes, which the README argues generalises across complex sites
One script can mix high-level tasks and low-level actions, and extract returns data validated against a zod schema
A test runner turns the same agent into visual assertions for web-app testing, installable with one command
weaknesses: The README says it needs a large visually grounded model and recommends Claude Sonnet 4 or Qwen-2.5VL 72B, so model cost and choice are narrow
The 94 percent WebVoyager figure is the maintainers' own claim, and the README lists deterministic caching as in progress
The default branch has not been pushed since February 2026
why_it_matters: A widely starred browser agent that bets on pixel-level vision and ties the agent loop to repeatable test-style automation.
